chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"I'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) is not valid for less than three days, and whoever performs i'tikaf must fast, and it is appropriate for the one performing i'tikaf, when he enters the state of i'tikaf, to make a condition (specify the duration), just as the one who enters the state of Ihram (for Hajj or Umrah) makes a condition."

key_terms.اَلِاعْتِكَافُ: I'tikaf: Spiritual seclusion in a mosque for worship
key_terms.ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Three days: The minimum duration for valid I'tikaf
key_terms.صَامَ: He fasted: The requirement of fasting during I'tikaf
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَ: He should stipulate: The recommendation to specify the duration of seclusion
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: He enters Ihram: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and minimum duration for I'tikaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the minimum duration of I'tikaf as three days, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of one day and emphasizing its status as a distinct act of worship rather than merely staying in the mosque. It mandates fasting as a condition for validity and draws a parallel to the ritual intention (niyyah) required in Hajj, highlighting the importance of precise contractual stipulation (shart) in Islamic devotional practices. This ruling underscores the seriousness of I'tikaf as a committed spiritual retreat, requiring both physical abstinence and focused devotion.
